body.statement: For fixed \(\mathcal A\), when \(L=0\), every feasible refinement is the translation closure of one finite static ADMG on \(V\), and \(\gamma=0\). The first two lag-one special branches of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)\) cannot match. If \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,0)\) holds, the procedure returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\), which is uniformly valid. Otherwise it makes one ordinary-ID call on the relevant ancestral subgraph. If ID succeeds, it returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), where \(F\) is the ordinary-ID functional on the common product alphabet; if ID fails, it returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). No fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is claimed on the ID-failure branch.
body.justification: At zero lag the success computation is exactly ordinary ID.
body.gap: ID failure returns unknown because the fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is unproved.
body.consumer: Static users recover valid ordinary-ID successes without an unsafe failure claim.
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(L=0\). Since \(0\leq\gamma\leq L\), necessarily \(\gamma=0\). By \(\mathrm{ass:refinement\text{-}span}\), every directed edge and every shared-root relation has offset zero. Stationarity of a refinement translates each such relation through all integer times, while \(\mathrm{ass:exact\text{-}summary}\) fixes its coordinate pair. Hence each feasible refinement is the translation closure of the finite static ADMG specified by \(H\). If the directed part of \(H\) contained a directed cycle or a directed self-loop, its time-zero copy would violate \(\mathrm{ass:instantaneous\text{-}acyclicity}\). Therefore \(H^{\to}\) is acyclic and loop-free.

The first two special rules of \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) require their displayed lag-one inputs, so neither matches an input with \(L=0\). There are now two cases. If
\[
 \mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,0)=\mathsf{true},
\]
the third rule returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\). Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}transfer}\) proves that this is a finite-cylinder functional and that
\[
 F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x)=\theta_M(y;x)
 \qquad(M\in\mathfrak M(H,0,\mathcal A)).
\]

If the adjustment predicate is false, the acyclic, loop-free property just proved forces the fourth rule to apply. At \(L=0\), the saturated time-unrolled ancestral graph has only time-zero vertices and is exactly the relevant ancestral subgraph of the static ADMG. The procedure makes its one memoized ordinary-ID call there. If ID returns \(F\), \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)
 =\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F),
 \qquad F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)
\]
for every compatible \(M\). If ID fails, the fourth rule returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). Thus a zero-lag input is handled by the earlier adjustment success when eligible and otherwise by exactly one ordinary-ID call; no failure of ID is converted into a fixed-alphabet stationary hedge certificate.
